items.title: Louis James Interview, 1959-05-25
items.q: You say you heard George Bocquet and he inspired you to take it up. That's right.

ctx.x: I played with Frankie Duesen and Jack Carey, you know. I played, you know, in the... What did you play then? Your... The spring clarinet. Your clarinet. Yeah, the spring clarinet. Then I made records with Louis Domaine, you know, with the tenor sax. Oh, yes.

Can you tell us about when you first took up the clarinet? You say you heard George Bocquet and he inspired you to take it up. Yeah, that's right. That's right. Where did you get the clarinet and when and all?

Well, I... I happened to buy a... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... A... And... Uh... I... 된... 된... 된... ! They bought me alto sax when I was playing clarinet. I pawned that and I never could get it out any time before I got it out. I pawned it one carnival. I didn't play, you know. I didn't worry about it. I couldn't get it out. So he just bought my ticket. Just like now, I'm playing clarinet, but you know, after I couldn't get going with a good…
